subject: Trial orientation: success criteria, timeline, and blocker log
messages:

Subject: Trial orientation: success criteria, timeline, and blocker log

Hi Emma / Rajesh —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our call and the proposed plan for the 4-week evaluation so your team can confirm: 

1) Success criteria (what OrbitHealth will evaluate)
- Latency: 95th percentile token latency under 250ms for typical clinical prompts (~150 tokens)
- Cost: average per-1k-token inference cost under $X (we will provide upfront estimates)
- Quality: pass rate >= 90% on the 25 internal prompts you shared (we'll run an automated scorer and a small human spot-check)
- Data safety: no PHI leakage on the test corpus; environment must meet your network/KMS requirements

2) Evaluation plan and ownership
- Week 0 (this week): onboarding, credentials, and baseline runs (owner: Priyom)
- Week 1: run automated prompt suite + initial human QA (owner: Monica)
- Week 2: performance tuning (batching/seq-length profiles) and attack-style PHI tests (owner: Monica + Neha)
- Week 3: production-readiness checklist, fallback policy test, and cost optimization recommendations (owner: Sean)
- Week 4: final scoring and go/no-go review with your stakeholders (owner: Priyom)

3) Immediate asks for OrbitHealth (please confirm by EOD tomorrow)
- Provide the finalized 25 prompt set and scoring rubric (if different from what you shared)
- Confirm whether you'll run on redwood hosted API or want a Private deployment for the trial
- Point of contact for procurement (we'll need an MSA/NDA path)

4) Known risks & mitigations (quick tracker)
- PHI concerns: mitigation = recommend Private deployment + KMS key control; if hosted, we will set up strict retention and audit hooks (owner: Neha)
- Network egress rules: we require the firewall rules below; if not permitted, there will be a fixed-delay for a Private deployment setup (owner: Priyom)
- Model edge cases for hallucination on clinical prompts: we will include guardrails and a small human-in-the-loop review for critical templates (owner: Monica)

Attachments: OrbitHealth_POC_Metrics.xlsx (baseline metrics template) and network_diagram_v2.pdf (recommended firewall/VPC rules)

Next steps: once you confirm the above items, we will provision access and schedule a 60-min onboarding for next Tuesday.

Thanks —
Priyom

Emma / team —

I ran a quick risk assessment after the call and want to flag one technical blocker that will require immediate attention during week 0:

1) Token-level PII leakage in batching path (blocking)
- Description: when using our continuous batching optimization with long prefix contexts, redaction heuristics can miss edge-case tokenization boundaries for clinician notes. We have an internal repro that shows PII strings appearing in intermediate caches under a specific tokenization pattern.
- Impact: potential PHI exposure in logs/trace if not mitigated — blocks trial on real data until addressed
- Immediate mitigations (week 0):
  a) Disable continuous KV cache for trial runs on real clinical snippets and switch to deterministic per-request cache (reduces throughput but safe)
  b) Enable strict token redaction pass before any logs are written; run a synthetic PII fuzz job on a sanitized sample provided by OrbitHealth
  c) Audit logs: ensure traces redact token buffers and store only hashed traces (owner: Neha)
- Escalation path: if mitigation (a)-(c) cannot be completed prior to onboarding, we will offer a synthetic-data-only trial and schedule a 72-hour patch window with infra (escalation contact: Neha Kapoor; backup: Monica Patel)

I'll also add the technical notes and the repro case to the Drive folder for your security team to review.

Neha Kapoor
Security Lead, Inference
